proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the true lag is longer/variable or admissions track a distinct hospitalized process, delayed_I may mis-time the peak and distort inferred growth/decline rates.
proposals.rationale: Weekly hospitalization rates can plausibly lag the infectious proxy; adding an exposed stage supports sharp, high-peaked waves while keeping the template parsimonious for a 31-week training window.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-smoothing or phase shift if the effective lag is closer to 0–1 weeks; may underfit shoulders if multiple sub-peaks exist.
proposals.rationale: A 2-week reporting/admission lag is a common coarse weekly-timescale approximation; SEIR helps represent rapid rise and fall consistent with high peakiness.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H may be weakly identifiable in a short single-season series, leading to parameter tradeoffs (I↔H) and unstable forecasts.
proposals.rationale: Directly mapping observations to an explicit hospitalized compartment aligns with the target semantics (hospitalization_rate) and can capture sharper peaks via an I→H flow without relying on an ad hoc delay.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If the data are truly admissions-only, I+H can bias amplitude and broaden peaks by attributing signal to I rather than H.
proposals.rationale: If surveillance reflects a mixture of infectious burden and admissions (e.g., coding/ascertainment blending), observing I+H can be a robust compromise while retaining hospitalization dynamics.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: With only ~41 weeks total, waning may be unidentifiable and can mimic noise or induce spurious secondary waves.
proposals.rationale: Allows waning immunity/re-susceptibility, which can help accommodate high-rate-scale series with potential within-season replenishment effects while still using a simple lagged observation.
